query: What documentaries have I watched?
notes: 'Documentary' isn't a genre present in the corpus at all -- ground truth is an empty list (ground_truth_call is kept so refresh_ground_truth.py still checks that data premise). Routing is free: checking get_all_genres and then search_my_history is as valid as filter_by_genre. Tests honest 'none found' instead of a fabricated or miscategorized answer. Graded manually: PASS if the answer says nothing in the watch history fits and presents no watched film AS a match; naming watched films explicitly to rule them out, or offering one clearly framed as related-but-not-a-match, is fine.

query: What Marvel movies did I really enjoy?
notes: 'Marvel' isn't a genre or any tool parameter -- forces a routing judgment call (likely search_my_history, or several actor/franchise lookups). Graded manually on whether the interpretation is reasonable and nothing is invented.

query: Search my history for something with a great plot twist, then run that exact same search again to double-check the results.
notes: Deliberately instructs a literal repeat -- checks that the step-14 duplicate-call guard actually engages rather than the model just complying and burning an iteration.

query: What werewolf movies have I seen?
notes: No werewolf film is in the watch history (verified during calibration labeling). search_my_history has no confidence gate and always returns its 8 closest films, so this tests whether the agent judges them from the evidence and says nothing fits instead of presenting near misses (e.g. The Wolf of Wall Street on a title-word match). Graded manually: PASS if the answer says nothing in the watch history fits and presents no watched film AS a match; naming watched films explicitly to rule them out, or offering one clearly framed as related-but-not-a-match, is fine.
